title: Travel Trouble
grammarNote: The simple future (hablaré, será, habrá, podré, tendré) states what will happen, and contrasts with the near-future 'voy a...' which implies an existing plan. The conditional (podría, sería) softens requests and hypotheticals, and phrases like 'el problema es que' and 'me temo que' frame a complaint politely.

phrases.target: Me temo que hay un problema con mi reservación
phrases.native: I'm afraid there's a problem with my reservation
phrases.phonetic: meh TEH-moh keh AHY oon proh-BLEH-mah kon mee reh-ser-vah-see-OHN
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Me temo que' (I'm afraid that) is a soft, polite way to introduce bad news or a complaint, common in service settings.

exampleSentence.target: Buenas tardes. Me temo que hay un problema con mi reservación.
exampleSentence.native: Good afternoon. I'm afraid there's a problem with my reservation.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Temo' is present tense, but the whole frame softens the statement much like 'I fear' does in English — useful for opening a complaint gently.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Temo' sounds like 'temo(r)', fear — you fear the bad news you're about to deliver.

phrases.target: El problema es que no aparece mi reservación en el sistema
phrases.native: The problem is that my reservation doesn't appear in the system
phrases.phonetic: el proh-BLEH-mah es keh noh ah-pah-REH-seh mee reh-ser-vah-see-OHN en el sees-TEH-mah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'El problema es que...' names the specific issue clearly after softening the complaint — pairs naturally with 'me temo que'.

exampleSentence.target: El problema es que no aparece mi reservación en el sistema.
exampleSentence.native: The problem is that my reservation doesn't appear in the system.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Es que' introduces an explanatory clause; it's a fixed frame for pinpointing the exact cause of trouble.
phrases.memoryHook: Think 'the problem IS that' — direct and factual, no softening needed once you've already opened politely.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: The problem is that my reservation doesn't appear in the system
practiceItems.answer: El problema es que no aparece mi reservación en el sistema

practiceItems.answer: No aparece mi reservación en el sistema

phrases.native: Could you offer me a similar room?
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Podría' is the conditional of 'poder', used to make a polite, softened request instead of a blunt command.

exampleSentence.target: ¿Podría ofrecerme una habitación similar en otro piso?
exampleSentence.native: Could you offer me a similar room on another floor?

phrases.grammarNote: The conditional 'podría' distances the request from a direct demand, similar to English 'could' vs. 'can'.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Podría' looks like 'poder' (to be able) plus '-ía' — the '-ía' ending softens it into a polite maybe.

phrases.target: Mañana llegaré temprano al aeropuerto por si acaso
phrases.native: Tomorrow I will arrive early at the airport just in case
phrases.phonetic: mah-NYAH-nah yeh-gah-REH tem-PRAH-noh al ah-eh-roh-PWEHR-toh por see ah-KAH-soh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Llegaré' is the simple future of 'llegar' (-é ending), stating a firm plan for tomorrow rather than a decision made just now.

exampleSentence.target: Mañana llegaré temprano al aeropuerto por si acaso hay retrasos.
exampleSentence.native: Tomorrow I will arrive early at the airport just in case there are delays.

phrases.grammarNote: Contrast the simple future 'llegaré' (a firm resolution about tomorrow) with 'voy a llegar', which would suggest a plan already decided moments ago.
phrases.memoryHook: The '-é' ending on 'llegaré' sounds like 'ay' — a confident 'I WILL arrive, no matter what'.
